avoid_supplements.name: Warfarin or other anticoagulants
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Additive anticoagulant effects and increased bleeding risk via platelet inhibition and displacement of warfarin from protein binding
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid concurrent use; if necessary, obtain INR monitoring and dose adjustment by prescriber

avoid_supplements.name: High-dose Vitamin E (>400 IU/day)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Potentiates antiplatelet effects and increases bleeding risk
avoid_supplements.action: Limit vitamin E intake to ≤400 IU/day or discontinue if bleeding risk concerns exist

avoid_supplements.name: Ginkgo biloba
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Inhibits platelet aggregation and increases bleeding risk when combined with aspirin's antiplatelet effects
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid concurrent use or monitor closely for signs of bleeding

avoid_supplements.name: Feverfew
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Potentiates antiplatelet effects and increases bleeding risk
avoid_supplements.action: Discontinue feverfew or separate dosing; consult healthcare provider

caution_supplements.name: Garlic supplement
caution_supplements.mechanism: May have mild antiplatelet properties and potentiate bleeding risk at high doses
caution_supplements.action: Monitor for unusual bruising or bleeding; use moderate amounts

caution_supplements.name: Turmeric/Curcumin
caution_supplements.mechanism: May have mild antiplatelet activity and increase bleeding risk at high doses
caution_supplements.action: Use dietary amounts; avoid high-dose supplements without medical supervision

caution_supplements.name: Ginger
caution_supplements.mechanism: Mild antiplatelet properties may potentiate aspirin effects at high doses
caution_supplements.action: Use culinary amounts; monitor for bleeding signs with high-dose supplements

avoid_foods.name: Alcohol (chronic heavy use)
avoid_foods.mechanism: Increases GI bleeding risk, inhibits platelet function, and increases aspirin's anticoagulant effects
avoid_foods.action: Limit alcohol to ≤1 drink/day for women, ≤2 drinks/day for men; avoid binge drinking

caution_foods.name: High-dose caffeine (>400 mg/day)
caution_foods.mechanism: May increase GI irritation when combined with aspirin
caution_foods.action: Limit caffeine intake; take aspirin with food and adequate water

caution_foods.name: Spicy foods
caution_foods.mechanism: May increase gastric irritation and dyspepsia when combined with aspirin
caution_foods.action: Consume spicy foods in moderation; take aspirin with meals

caution_foods.name: Fatty/fried foods
caution_foods.mechanism: May delay aspirin absorption and increase GI upset
caution_foods.action: Take aspirin with light meals; avoid high-fat foods immediately after dosing

monitoring_notes: Monitor for signs of GI bleeding (melena, hematemesis, abdominal pain) and unusual bruising or bleeding, especially in patients on concurrent anticoagulants or antiplatelet agents. Assess renal function periodically as NSAIDs can impair renal perfusion; use lowest effective dose for shortest duration, particularly in elderly patients and those with cardiovascular or renal disease.
